evals.prompt: Audit the next user-facing page in this application. The UI tree and audit progress documents already exist. Inspect the page and its backend integration, fix all valid findings, add missing focused tests, run the relevant test suite, build, and Playwright Chromium checks, update progress, commit the iteration, then report what changed and ask whether to continue.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator confirms the mode with the user (or defaults to auto-fix), reads both documents, selects one work unit, delegates to Section Auditor, blocks the commit if validation fails, otherwise updates progress and creates one scoped commit before pausing.

evals.prompt: Start the audit loop in this project. There is no UI tree document and no audit progress document yet. Map the frontend and backend integration first, create the required documents, then audit only the first meaningful page or SPA view and stop after one validated iteration.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator asks the mode question first, delegates tree creation to Tree Mapper, creates or initializes progress state, delegates exactly one work unit to Section Auditor, and does not continue automatically.

evals.prompt: Run one audit-loop iteration, but the repository already contains unrelated uncommitted changes. Do not overwrite, stage, or commit them. Explain what must happen before the loop can safely proceed.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator stops at the clean-tree precondition and does not delegate fixes or create a commit.

evals.prompt: Perform a complete project-wide UI/backend wiring audit in one run, and fix everything you find automatically without asking me about individual findings. Do not stop after the first page or first batch of findings. Build a global inventory and state matrix for every route, control, data-bearing element, role, empty/error/loading state, privacy setting, cache path, pagination path, relation, lifecycle transition, and browser flow; trace every read and write end to end; record confirmed, intentional, missing-coverage, and unproven results; then repair and validate all confirmed in-scope findings.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator asks the mode question first, the user selects auto-fix, and discovery completes across all mapped units before repair. It reports a finding ledger with evidence and proof status, runs relevant tests and project-local production Chromium/CDP harnesses, distinguishes implementation failures from environment gaps, updates both audit documents, and does not ask to continue until the full-sweep completion criteria are met.

evals.prompt: Run a complete project-wide audit, but do not change any code during the audit. After discovery is finished, walk me through every confirmed defect one at a time: explain each issue, show me a table with its severity, location, description, impact, evidence, and recommendation, offer your proposed fix, and let me decide what to do before you move to the next one.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator asks the mode question first, the user selects interactive mode. Discovery runs across all mapped units with code untouched. Then the orchestrator presents a severity-grouped summary table of the full ledger, then walks through each finding one at a time with a per-issue detail table and a four-option decision prompt (proposed solution / different approach / skip / already resolved), fixes and verifies only what the user approves, records a terminal status for every finding, and reports the final ledger.

evals.prompt: Audit the whole project and fix everything automatically. I do not want to review each finding.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator confirms the mode, the user selects auto-fix, and the run proceeds with discovery then autonomous repair, verification, and a final complete report without per-finding prompts.

evals.prompt: Run a live user flow audit against the deployed app. The site is at my production domain and I can give you shell access to the host that runs it. Go through every feature end to end and fix whatever is broken — I don't want to review anything until you're done.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator asks the mode questions, then enforces the chunking rule: it runs preflight (live URL, host access, deployed revision, identities, data-safety contract, server-side observation recipes, browser runtime, baseline health), writes the full flow inventory and a numbered chunk plan, executes only chunk 1, fixes confirmed defects in place, and stops for a go sign with a chunk report and next-chunk list. It does not run unattended through the remaining chunks.

evals.prompt: A booking form silently fails on the live site — the browser shows a success toast but the appointment never appears. Use the host to find out why.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator treats the browser symptom and the host observation as one investigation: it reproduces the flow live, then uses the validated recipes (service logs at the request timestamp, row state, queue, cache) to establish the ordering failure, confirms the defect host-side before recording it, records it with a stable ID, fixes it in the repository rather than on the host, and reports it as awaiting live verification until it is deployed and the flow re-run.

evals.prompt: The live flow audit is at a chunk boundary. Finish it in this session, don't stop to ask me, just run the rest of the chunks.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator honors the request to keep going but still emits a report at every chunk boundary, and still checkpoints the state file so each boundary is resumable. It does not skip the boundary itself.

evals.prompt: Open a fresh session and continue the live user flow audit from where the last session stopped.
evals.expected_output: With no conversational memory, the orchestrator reads docs/live-flow-audit.md, confirms the live URL, host, deployed revision, identities, data-safety contract, flow verdicts so far, defect ledger statuses, and cleanup state, then starts exactly the chunk named in the Next up block at the flow it names — without re-running completed chunks and without re-asking settled questions.
